metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth degradation waste GPU compute hours before they cause visible outages, making them the leading indicator of data center health for AI workloads.

Distributed AI training synchronizes gradients across many GPUs in lockstep. When the internal fabric or external transit degrades even slightly, some GPUs stall waiting for others to finish their compute. A 5% packet loss does not cause 5% downtime; it causes 50% or more of the GPUs to sit idle during each synchronization step. This is why facilities tracking only SLA uptime compliance miss the real cost. A network running at specification uptime can still bleed compute efficiency through latency creep or intermittent loss that never triggers an alert.

Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization catches this waste before it becomes catastrophic. The metric covers both internal fabric (the switches and cables between GPUs in the same facility) and external transit (the pipes to other facilities or customer connections). Each is a separate failure mode. This data does not capture application-layer issues, redundancy of the measurement system itself, or whether the facility takes action on the data it collects. It also does not specify the thresholds that trigger remediation, which vary widely by workload.
